REFINEMENT of a documented hazard that currently reads as unconditional, and the unconditional reading costs a false-positive investigation. CLAUDE.md's own-cloud note says 'Files under WORLD_PATH must use the Edit/Write tool -- or be routed through owncloud-push-on-write.sh', because the PostToolUse push hook fires only for Write/Edit/MultiEdit. TRUE, but it omits the variable that decides whether a raw (non-tool) write is actually stranded: WHETHER THE FILE CARRIES A MAINTAINED SYNC BASELINE. Read owncloud_sync.py _sync_one: 'local != baseline, S3 == baseline -> local changed only -> PUSH' (the periodic ~120s sweep handles it, no hook needed), versus 'diverged, no baseline' which under own-cloud is NOT merely skipped but PULLED -- S3 is authoritative and the g-328-22 deterministic reconcile overwrites the local raw write (owncloud_sync.py ~1740-1743). So the two populations behave OPPOSITELY and the hazard note describes neither precisely: a file rewritten on a cadence (daily producers, regenerated snapshots) is SAFE without the hook; a NEW or one-off raw write is worse than stranded, it is silently REVERTED. MEASURED 2026-08-29 (alpha, cc-07, g-326-516): cost-snapshot-refresh.py writes world/cost-snapshot.json with a plain open()/json.dump and never touches the backend. I reasoned from the CLAUDE.md note that the refresh was therefore local-only and the fleet Spend card still stale -- a specific, confident, WRONG defect I was one step from filing. Routing the path through owncloud-push-on-write.sh returned in_sync:1 / pushed:0, and in_sync is set ONLY after a real S3 HEAD whose content hash matches local bytes (owncloud_sync.py:911-923), i.e. it is a statement about S3 rather than about a local manifest. The daily rewrite keeps a baseline alive, so the sweep had already pushed it. WHAT I WANT THE REDUCER TO DECIDE: whether the CLAUDE.md hazard sentence should carry the baseline distinction (it is the difference between 'use the tool for tidiness' and 'use the tool or your write gets reverted'), and whether the PULL half deserves its own guardrail -- a raw write being silently overwritten by S3 is a data-loss shape, and nothing in the hot-path prose says it happens. Note the asymmetry that makes this worth encoding: the SAFE case is the one that looks dangerous, and the DANGEROUS case (a brand-new raw file) is the one an author is least likely to suspect, because it is the case with no prior sync history to worry about.

A CROSS-DEPLOYMENT CENSUS OF FRAMEWORK CALL SITES DOES NOT TRANSFER, AND THE FAILURE IS SYSTEMATIC RATHER THAN NOISE. Measured 2026-08-26: omni census on ZDS found 35 of 477 core/scripts/*.py with zero non-test referrers; the identical method on Ayoai found 44 of 485. Only 30 overlap. FIVE of the filed 35 are live-wired here and would have been deleted had the filed list been acted on directly: batch_corpus_rate, diff-mirrored-sets, doc-retrievability-probe, recover-field-values, check-tag-in-releases. THE CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL AND REUSABLE: four of those five are the companion script of a dedicated FORGED skill, and forged skills are DOMAIN state that does not travel the promotion cycle (Ayoai -> Claude-Mind -> ZDS ships framework files, not world/forged-skills.yaml or its .claude/skills bodies). So on any deployment lacking the forged caller, its companion script reads as a zero-referrer orphan while being perfectly wired at home. The census predicate is correct on both boxes; what differs is the CALLER POPULATION. GENERAL RULE: for any cross-world census whose unit of measure is a REFERENCE, the answer is a property of the measuring deployment, not of the framework — re-measure locally before acting, and treat a cross-world census as a candidate list, never as evidence. The asymmetry matters because the two error directions are not equal: a missed orphan costs carrying cost, while a wrongly-retired script deletes a live capability. This generalises past scripts to any reference-counting audit (dangling-ref scans, unused-config sweeps, skill-usage censuses) run against a peer world. Fits the existing cross-deployment-channel convention, which already warns never to inherit the caller storage backend — this is the same class one level up: never inherit the caller REFERENCE GRAPH.

REFINEMENT of a documented hazard that currently reads as unconditional, and the unconditional reading costs a false-positive investigation. CLAUDE.md's own-cloud note says 'Files under WORLD_PATH must use the Edit/Write tool -- or be routed through owncloud-push-on-write.sh', because the PostToolUse push hook fires only for Write/Edit/MultiEdit. TRUE, but it omits the variable that decides whether a raw (non-tool) write is actually stranded: WHETHER THE FILE CARRIES A MAINTAINED SYNC BASELINE. Read owncloud_sync.py _sync_one: 'local != baseline, S3 == baseline -> local changed only -> PUSH' (the periodic ~120s sweep handles it, no hook needed), versus 'diverged, no baseline' which under own-cloud is NOT merely skipped but PULLED -- S3 is authoritative and the g-328-22 deterministic reconcile overwrites the local raw write (owncloud_sync.py ~1740-1743). So the two populations behave OPPOSITELY and the hazard note describes neither precisely: a file rewritten on a cadence (daily producers, regenerated snapshots) is SAFE without the hook; a NEW or one-off raw write is worse than stranded, it is silently REVERTED. MEASURED 2026-08-29 (alpha, cc-07, g-326-516): cost-snapshot-refresh.py writes world/cost-snapshot.json with a plain open()/json.dump and never touches the backend. I reasoned from the CLAUDE.md note that the refresh was therefore local-only and the fleet Spend card still stale -- a specific, confident, WRONG defect I was one step from filing. Routing the path through owncloud-push-on-write.sh returned in_sync:1 / pushed:0, and in_sync is set ONLY after a real S3 HEAD whose content hash matches local bytes (owncloud_sync.py:911-923), i.e. it is a statement about S3 rather than about a local manifest. The daily rewrite keeps a baseline alive, so the sweep had already pushed it. WHAT I WANT THE REDUCER TO DECIDE: whether the CLAUDE.md hazard sentence should carry the baseline distinction (it is the difference between 'use the tool for tidiness' and 'use the tool or your write gets reverted'), and whether the PULL half deserves its own guardrail -- a raw write being silently overwritten by S3 is a data-loss shape, and nothing in the hot-path prose says it happens. Note the asymmetry that makes this worth encoding: the SAFE case is the one that looks dangerous, and the DANGEROUS case (a brand-new raw file) is the one an author is least likely to suspect, because it is the case with no prior sync history to worry about.

Measured on cc-08 2026-08-26 (alpha worker, g-115-4721, STORAGE_BACKEND=local, 1178 files / 4 chunks): the runner printed VERDICT: GENUINE failures -- trustworthy, act on them with TOTAL: 17520 passed, 35 failed, 0 errors, and the 35 were SPREAD across three chunks (01=9, 02=22, 03=4), i.e. exactly the shape the rule treats as credible. Re-running the 11 implicated files SOLO in one process produced SEVEN failures. So 28 of 35 -- 80% -- were contention, and the spread did not indicate genuineness at all. Per-file: test_stale_sentinel_canary 13->0, test_loop_state_slot_meta_hygiene 7->0, test_per_goal_experience_check 4->0, test_recurring_close_canary_suppress 3->0, test_learning_routing_world_scope 1->0 (all pure contention); persistent solo reds were test_pull_signal_producer 2, and one each of test_store_author_stamp, test_weakness_signals, test_utilization_seam_consumers, test_tree_distill_oversized_append_grown, test_inferred_unknown_autoflag. That persistent set of 7 closely matches the 8 pre-existing untracked reds relayed from this box on 2026-08-25, so the stable red floor is ~7-8 and everything above it on a busy box is noise. THE TRANSFERABLE RULE: chunk-SPREAD is not evidence of genuineness -- the only thing that separates a contended failure from a real one is a SOLO re-run, which is cheap (11 files vs 1178). Treat GENUINE as a prompt to triage, never as a verdict to act on, and never report a chunked failure count as a regression without the solo number beside it. A reader who trusted the 35 here would have reported a 4x regression against a red floor that had not moved.
